thread:
marta: Heads-up — noticed a customer hit where a streaming request that included a toolcall retried mid-stream and the console shows double-charging for the same logical completion. Filing here to get platform eyes.

kevin: Oof. Do you have repro steps or logs? Is this the hosted API or dedicated?

marta: Hosted. Quick repro (sanitized): user sends streaming generation, at token ~120 they trigger a toolcall which causes the server to return an intermediate 'tool_response' and then subsequent generator frames continue. A retry happened after an upstream timeout and the client reconnected; server replayed chunks and billing shows both streams as charged. Logs: 

```
request_id=abc-123 pid=grpc-7 frame_seq=1 tokens=50 event=stream_chunk
request_id=abc-123 pid=grpc-7 frame_seq=2 tokens=70 event=toolcall
request_id=abc-123 pid=grpc-7 frame_seq=3 tokens=30 event=stream_chunk
--- client reconnect (retry) ---
request_id=abc-123 pid=grpc-12 frame_seq=1 tokens=50 event=stream_chunk
request_id=abc-123 pid=grpc-12 frame_seq=2 tokens=70 event=toolcall
request_id=abc-123 pid=grpc-12 frame_seq=3 tokens=30 event=stream_chunk
billing: charged 220 then charged 220 (total 440)
```

marta: Looks like billing is naive per-frame accounting without cross-request dedupe.

samir: Thanks for the dump. I think root cause: we attribute tokens at emission time per chunk and aren't checking for idempotency across reconnects. For unary requests we use an idempotency key but streaming chunks don't carry a persistent id.

leila: We also need to consider truncation: if a truncate (client or server) happens after toolcall, the final frame might be shorter and billing should only charge what actually persisted. Right now we charge all emitted frames even if they were aborted by truncation/retry.

kevin: Proposed quick fixes: (A) add chunk-level idempotency token (stream_chunk_id) and maintain a short-lived seen set keyed by (request_id, chunk_id) before billing; (B) only finalize billing on terminal events (stream_end, tool_result_commit) and keep provisional counters for in-flight frames. Thoughts?

samir: (A) is simpler and less invasive. (B) is safer but requires changing billing semantics and also UI wiring. If we keep provisional counters, console quotas may look weird until finalized.

marta: Example wire change I sketched:

```
stream_send({
  request_id: "abc-123",
  chunk_id: "c-0001",
  payload: "...",
  event_type: "stream_chunk"
})
```

server will ignore duplicate (request_id, chunk_id) for billing and processing.

kevin: Caveat: if clients retry and re-use same chunk ids but server lost state (evicted seen set), duplicates may still charge. We need TTL long enough for typical retry windows (say 60s) and eviction metrics.

leila: Also add UI telemetry: quota-breakdown should expose a "deduped_stream_tokens" metric to show when dedupe prevented charging. Ops teams will want to see that.

ops-bot: incident-alert: spike in billing_charges_per_request on 2026-03-12 14:21 UTC — correlated with increased client disconnects in us-west-2.

billing-bot: note: there are existing customers flagged for double charge refunds. We'll need a retroactive reconciliation if we can't guarantee dedupe for past events.

samir: Implementation plan suggestion: 1) wire chunk_id (client-side) + server-side seen-set with TTL 120s; 2) metric counter for deduped tokens and a console panel; 3) fallback policy: if no chunk_id present, continue existing behavior but emit a warning in logs and telemetry; 4) long-term: consider finalization semantics for billing.

kevin: I'll own a small RFC: add chunk_id to streaming protocol + billing dedupe table. Will prototype dedupe cache in the routing layer (fast path) so we don't incur extra DB latency.

marta: :+1: thanks. For immediate customer relief, ops will run reconciliation and issue credits where obvious duplicates match request_id + identical token totals. Please add reconciliation checklist to the ticket.

leila: Also pinging UX to add a console badge for "deduped tokens" so SREs notice when this mitigation is working.

kevin: Filed RFC PR -> will drop the link here once ready.

marta: Thanks everyone. Follow-ups: RFC, reconciliation run, small dashboard panel.

kevin: quick note — include test cases for kv-eviction (seqs re-sent after eviction) so we don't accidentally under-charge when client legitimately replays.

marta: Agree. I'll add test matrix.

kevin: any objections to rolling the dedupe cache to 120s TTL and adding a feature-flag for the billing logic?

samir: No objections. Feature flag for 2 weeks, monitor deduped_stream_tokens and billing_delta.

marta: Cool. Thanks.
